findings.element: RevRec · Schedule start date confirmation modal → Schedule details table
findings.finding: The modal says existing schedules keep their dates, but after Confirm the existing sub_after_release_3c1b row's Schedule start changes from 28 Dec 2025 to 6 Jan 2026 (or to Payment date), so the reassurance turns out to be false.
findings.user_impact: A nervous owner who clicked Confirm because they were told nothing old would change sees an existing schedule re-dated, stops trusting the setting and the product, and is afraid to touch anything else.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the table match the promise and leave existing rows unchanged after Confirm (only new schedules use the new start date), so the "keep their current dates" reassurance is true on screen.

evidence.quote: The new Schedule start date applies going forward only. Existing recognition schedules keep their current dates.
evidence.source: plain-language: reassurance must match what the screen then shows (missing/false reassurance)

findings.element: PT · Invoices tab · Invoice date select help text
findings.finding: "Created" and "issued" read as the same thing to a non-accountant, and the copy never says what the choice changes in the books (which month the invoice and its revenue land in).
findings.user_impact: The owner cannot tell which option is right for them, so they guess or leave the default and never learn that "Created date" can put revenue into an earlier, possibly already-closed month.
findings.suggested_fix: Explain the 2 dates and what each does in plain words. Issued date is the "Date of issue" on the invoice, when the customer owes you. Then add one short line on what changes, for example: "The date your books use for the invoice."

evidence.quote: Select which date Synder posts Stripe invoices under in your books — Created date, when Stripe created the invoice, or Issued date, when the invoice was issued to the customer.
evidence.source: plain-language (unexplained term "issued"; also uses "posts" where vocabulary.md says "Sync (Synchronization) | post, push")

findings.element: Summary Sync · Sales recording date help text, second sentence
findings.finding: The sentence is engineering/spec wording: "the issued option", "Datasource dating" and "Per Transaction rules" mean nothing to a business owner.
findings.user_impact: The owner starts to wonder whether they are missing something important about which date to pick, then gives up on the help text and picks blindly.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the sentence, or replace it with a plain fact such as "Uses the same dates as Per Transaction Sync."

evidence.quote: Default for the issued option is Invoice issued date. Datasource dating matches Per Transaction rules.
evidence.source: unexplained jargon (plain-language); vocabulary.md Product Names: "Per Transaction Sync"

gaps: Sync info / transaction drilldown is not in the prototype, so I could not check whether an owner can tell that the accounting date differs from the created date shown in the transactions table (FDD S1.5)
"Learn more →" and "How to change mode" links go to href="#", so I could not check whether they explain created vs issued or the consequences
"Upgrade plan" links do nothing, so the below-Pro upgrade path cannot be checked for discoverability
Trial and new-connection states were never shown, and pt-pro does not say whether it is a new or existing connection. I could not check whether the default caption matches what the user actually sees

After an Invoice date change, "Update" → "Settings updated" coexists with the auto-save toast "Saved". Whether the first change was really saved without Update was not confirmed (for example by reloading), so this anxiety point is not verified
